text: This week in New England brings a bittersweet mixture of nostalgia and uncertainty as the Patriots prepare for their Week 2 home opener against the Steelers on Sunday at 1 PM ET. Stephon Gilmore, the two-time All-Pro cornerback and 2019 NFL Defensive Player of the Year, signed a one-day contract Friday to retire as a Patriot, cementing his legacy as one of the greatest defensive backs in franchise history, while the team simultaneously grapples with potential depth concerns in the secondary with starting cornerback Carlton Davis III listed as questionable for the matchup. On the injury front, running back TreVeyon Henderson appears to have cleared the most significant hurdle after missing the opener with an ankle injury, telling reporters Thursday he's "ready to go" for Sunday's contest. Meanwhile, the organization made headlines off the field when Patriots owner Robert Kraft announced he had Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming Gillette Stadium shows, citing the artist's "history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery," and in a lighter promotional note, Hall of Famer Adam Vinatieri will attempt a Guinness World Record kick at Jungfraujoch in the Swiss Alps as part of the Patriots' marketing push for their upcoming game in Munich.
